lesson.menu_title: Networking Mastery -- The Welcome Reception in Miami
lesson.menu_desc: Meet, impress and keep in touch with the people of your cohort at the welcome reception of the Miami module -- use networking phrasal verbs and put the object pronoun in the right place (set it up / run into him) -- 39 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 26 -- Networking Mastery
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Nilo Mesquita Patussi | Lesson 26 -- Networking Mastery
lesson.grammar_point: phrasal verbs (separable and inseparable, object pronoun position)

listenings.text: Hello, Doctor Nilo, it's Sofia from the program office. Just a quick message about tonight. The welcome reception starts at seven p.m. on the hotel terrace, and it finishes at ten. About sixty people will be there: the participants of your cohort, the lecturers of the Miami module, and some guests from American clubs. Please bring your business cards, but don't hand out too many. The best idea is to choose a few people and have real conversations. I will set up two short introductions for you: one with the head of the Rabat module, and one with a lawyer from a club in Los Angeles. If you have any problems tonight, just look for me near the entrance. And one more thing: the dress code is business casual, so no tie. See you on the terrace.

Hi Nilo, it's Daniel, your mentor. I heard that you hit it off with some people at the reception last night. Well done. Now comes the part that most people forget: the follow-up. Here is my advice. Today or tomorrow, send a short message to each person you met. Don't write a long email. Remind them where you met, mention one thing that you talked about, and suggest a next step. For example, you can set up a fifteen-minute call, or you can offer to pass on an article. When I was in your cohort, I met a sports lawyer from Spain at the reception. We kept in touch, and two years later, we worked together on a big transfer case. So remember: a contact is not a card in your pocket. A contact is a relationship that you look after. Talk to you on Thursday.
